info.title: Road Sign Math API
info.summary: The signs, the map and the players of Road Sign Math.
info.description: Every public sign, the ways people found to make it true, the map and who’s playing, read by anyone; sign-in by email, your own account, and posting signs and ways from the app. Answers are JSON in UTF-8 with snake_case keys and carry an `API-Version` header. A request with a token is never cached. An error is `{"error": {"code", "message"}}`.

A page of at most `limit` signs (default 20, at most 50). Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; it is null on the last.

post.description: Posts the uploaded photos with the numbers you checked, where and when you found it, who found it (you, unless you say), and optionally the first way to make it true. Without a way it is posted unsolved. `unlocked` lists the badges the post earned you. Our moderator looks first: a post that is clearly objectionable is held, and only you see it, with `moderation_note` saying why. The moderator also writes each photo’s alt text. You need a name first. At most 20 a day.

get.description: Badges are little road signs a player collects for what happened on the road: a new state, a square root, a sign found a year after the first. Nothing is added up or compared. A secret badge gives only its id and shelf. A player’s earned badges are in `GET /players/{handle}` and `GET /me`.

post.description: Sends a link that opens the app and a 6-digit code, both good for 15 minutes. The answer is the same whether or not the address has an account; the first sign-in makes one. At most 5 emails an hour to an address.

delete.description: Deletes your account and everything it made: the signs you posted (with every way and heart on them), the ways you found and the hearts you gave on other signs, your name among a sign’s finders, and your email. It can’t be undone. A 503 means a heart couldn’t be taken back just now and nothing more was deleted; try again in a minute. A 409 means one of your hearts was changing; try again.

post.description: The body is the photo itself, JPEG, PNG or WebP, at most 4 MB. It is kept at two sizes with its metadata (and so its location) removed. Send the answer’s `id` in `photo_ids` when posting, within a day. At most 60 a day.

post.summary: Add another way to make a sign true
post.description: The math must be true, and every number in it must be one of the sign’s numbers, each used no more often than the sign shows it. A way someone already found is a conflict. Answers with the sign, all its ways, and in `unlocked` the badges the way earned you. You need a name first. At most 100 a day.

put.description: One heart per player per sign; hearting it again changes nothing. Only a shown sign can be hearted. Answers with `hearted` and the sign’s `hearts`, which counts the website’s hearts too (null when the count can’t be read just now). A 503 means the heart couldn’t be counted and nothing changed. At most 200 hearts given or taken back a day.

post.description: Up to 20 screen views at once, each the path of the website page it matches (`/`, `/map`, `/signs/<slug>`, `/players/<handle>`) or a short one of its own (`/capture`): lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most two parts. They are counted in the site’s analytics as the app’s, with the request’s User-Agent and country and nothing about who sent them; signed in or not makes no difference. The answer comes once they are passed on, or a moment later if the counter is slow; a view that can’t be counted is dropped. At most 120 batches an hour from one network.

CatalogBadge.description: A badge in the catalog. Each shelf is drawn as a family of road signs.

secret.description: A secret badge gives only its id and shelf until someone earns it.

anyOf.description: How it is earned, in a line.
What its sign shows: a word, a symbol or a number.
For a badge earned in steps, each step’s count.

EarnedBadge.description: A badge a player earned, with the sign that earned it first. Badges follow the signs on the map, so one goes when its sign does.

mark.description: What its sign shows; a stepped badge shows its step.

anyOf.description: The step reached, for a badge earned in steps.

earned_on.description: The day the sign was found, or for the math, the day the way was written.

unlocked.description: Badges this post or way earned you just now, or a higher step of one.

needs_name.description: True until you give a name; ask for one before posting.

found_on.description: The day it was found, in your own time.

finders.description: Who found it: a player by handle, or a name for someone who doesn’t play. Default: you.

way.description: The first way to make it true, as math text. Leave it out to post unsolved.

anyOf.description: The sign’s hearts now; null when they can’t be counted just now.

login_id.description: Send it back with the code or the link’s token.

expires_in.description: Seconds the link and code work for.

token.description: The `t` parameter of the link in the email.
